A Administrative fee A percentage markup a landlord adds to the operating-expense pool to compensate for administering it, charged on top of expenses the tenant is already reimbursing. Alternative rent A lease provision that allows rent to be calculated using a different methodology — often reduced rent — when specified conditions occur. Artificial breakpoint A negotiated sales threshold above which a tenant begins paying percentage rent, set below the natural breakpoint rather than calculated from it. Attornment A tenant's agreement to recognize a new property owner or lender as its landlord following a foreclosure, transfer or similar event. B Base year The reference year used to determine which operating expense increases a tenant is responsible for under certain commercial leases. C CAM cap A limit on how much certain common area maintenance expenses can increase over time. Capital expenditure recovery The circumstances in which a landlord may pass some or all of a capital improvement cost through to tenants. Co-tenancy A lease clause that gives a tenant specific rights when required occupancy conditions at a shopping center or property are not maintained. Controllable expenses Operating costs that a lease classifies as being within the landlord's ability to manage or control. D Dark clause A clause addressing whether a tenant may stop operating from its leased premises while continuing to pay rent. Downstream cap A CAM cap that generally applies after operating expenses have been calculated or allocated to a tenant.
